Matt H: Hey team — first day setup question. I installed the WireGuard profile from infra and connected, public web works but I can't SSH to dev-bastion at 10.20.5.2 or curl any internal service (10.20.x.x). Who should I ping for access?
Sarah I (eng-infra): Welcome Matt! Quick checks: what's the VPN-assigned IP and can you paste `ifconfig` and a `traceroute 10.20.5.2`? Also try `dig @10.100.0.2 internal.service.redwood` if you have the internal DNS IP.
Matt H: Assigned IP is 172.16.50.12. Traceroute:
```
traceroute to 10.20.5.2 (10.20.5.2), 64 hops max, 52 byte packets
 1  172.16.50.1  1.123 ms  0.987 ms  1.052 ms
 2  * * *
```
`dig @10.100.0.2 internal.service.redwood` times out. Public DNS works. macOS Ventura on M1.
Jamie (sre): Sounds like either the split-tunnel policy didn't include the 10.20.0.0/16 routes or DNS isn't being pushed. Can you paste the WG config comment header (infra usually adds pushed-routes list)? If not, run `sudo route -n get 10.20.5.2` and `scutil --dns` output.
Matt H: Pasting `sudo route -n get 10.20.5.2` output:
```
route to: 10.20.5.2
destination: 10.20.5.2
interface: utun2
  type: UTUN
  gateway: 172.16.50.1
```
But traceroute still stops after the first hop. `scutil --dns` shows no 10.100.0.2 entry.
Sarah I (eng-infra): Ok that confirms DNS wasn't pushed. Two paths: infra can update the client config to push the internal DNS and routes, or you can add a local resolver file until we fix the profile. On mac, try: 
```
sudo mkdir -p /etc/resolver
echo 'nameserver 10.100.0.2' | sudo tee /etc/resolver/redwood
```
Then `dscacheutil -flushcache` and retry `dig internal.service.redwood @10.100.0.2`. If DNS was the only blocker, curl/ssh should start resolving to 10.20.x addresses.
Jamie (sre): If DNS fix doesn't help, ensure the split-tunnel includes 10.20.0.0/16. As a temporary workaround you can add a host route: 
```
sudo route -n add -net 10.20.0.0/16 172.16.50.1
```
(note: on mac route syntax uses net/mask like above). This forces traffic for 10.20.x onto the VPN utun gateway.
Matt H: Tried the resolver file, `dig internal.service.redwood @10.100.0.2` now returns the correct A record 10.20.12.8 but `ssh ubuntu@10.20.12.8` still times out. Ran the route add command and now SSH connects.
sec-bot: Security note — we saw your client IP 172.16.50.12 trying to access prod-like CIDR. We only allow 172.16.50.0/24 in the dev SGs. If you need broader access infra will file a short approval.
Sarah I (eng-infra): Thanks — Jamie, can you confirm split-tunnel/push policy? I'll update the WireGuard profile to include DNS 10.100.0.2 and the 10.20.0.0/16 route so new hires don't need manual steps.
Jamie (sre): On it. I updated the profile routing tags and pushed a config update — should be immediate but clients must reconnect. Also added a fallback to push DNS on recon.
Matt H: Reconnected and everything works now — can SSH and access internal dashboards. Huge help, thanks! :tada:
Sarah I (eng-infra): Welcome aboard! If you hit anything else ping #eng-infra or @infra-bot for the automated profile reissue. :wave:
